common_prompt:
Create ONE wholly new contemporary sacred PAINTING, vertical 4:5. Use the supplied images as references for abstract spatial omission and compositional omission ONLY. Override their blue palette with the neutral and slightly warm colors specified below. They are not edit targets. Do not preserve or recolor either composition. Do not reproduce their child, adult faces, costumes or gestures. Begin on a fresh canvas. Make the human relationship in the verified subject data the reason for every compositional decision.

ART DIRECTION: a present-day gallery painting in which recognizable people emerge through large interrupted fields of paint. Space is constructed from asymmetrical overlapping masses, passages of thin translucent paint, a few confidently drawn contours and selective sharply lit edges. Architecture and clothing become unresolved shapes. Do not insert conventionally rendered biblical actors in front of a geometric backdrop: figures and surrounding negative shapes must be conceived as one arrangement. Make some edges vanish into a neighboring color and recover elsewhere. Keep the faces and anatomical connections legible. No literal period set, meticulous village, theatrical costume tableau, illustration vignette, collage, decorative border or poster layout.

HUMAN PAINTING: clearly hand-painted faces and hands, even at close viewing. Model the curved eyelids, cheek and fingers with supple blended brush drawing and unexpected but coherent warm/cool pigment transitions. Show complete eyes, iris direction and gentle individual expressions with a few assured marks, not pores, eyelashes, lens sharpness or every hair. Never erase the eyes or turn the face into flat polygon masks. No photographic fragments. Paint the clothing more broadly than the skin, yet both visibly belong to the same brush and pigment. No all-over flakes, fish scales, patchwork impasto or texture-filter coating. Most large color fields are calm, thin and matte; concentrate visible, varied brushwork only where it describes form.

LIGHT AND COLOR: a neutral atmosphere with a slight living warmth. Ivory and warm stone light, restrained dusty rose, deep aubergine and charcoal. A little muted gray-lilac may balance the warmth. Avoid an orange, yellow or peach wash across the picture. Avoid a cold blue identity, antique brown varnish, sugary pastels and gray haze. Use a dramatic concentration of light against spacious shadows, not decorative rays, heaven clouds, halos or glitter. Warmth comes principally from attention between people, not a hot color filter.

MEANING: the highlighted Gospel words must be immediately sensed in gaze, posture, placement, gesture or the viewer's position. Do not default to blank faces or stock smiles. Keep all visible eyes, mouths, hands and bodily connections natural and complete. Abstract the room and peripheral clothes, not living anatomy. No horror, corpse-like skin, giant foreground anatomy or winged decoration. The painting is complete without any text, logo, signature, frame or reserved text area. All later revisions also require a newly generated painting, never an edit of a candidate image.

A.direction: A / WIDE. Compose a spatial encounter with relatively small but readable people. Let the placement of light, the distance between people and one interrupted architectural shape carry the meaning. A large quiet chromatic passage should be part of the composition, not an empty wall. Faces and hands remain anatomically complete at their natural scale. Do not reuse the reference layout or characters.

B.direction: B / CLOSE. Build an intimate, boldly cropped human encounter around a gaze or gesture meaningful to the verse. Let the expressive features be fully present and sensitively modeled in mixed pigment. The emotional connection is the focal point; the surrounding shapes are calm and spare. Use the references only for space and color relationships, not their subject scale or surface detail. No portrait collage.

C.direction: C / DISTINCT VIEWPOINT. Put the viewer in a meaningful position within the exchange, using a partial view, an unusual overlap or a reflection only when it serves this verse. Build a new arrangement rather than another crop of A or B. Keep the people alive and legible while the incomplete space leaves room for contemplation. No automatic reaching hand toward the lens, ghost figures or giant foreground anatomy.
